title: Client libraries and the REST API underneath everything

videos.script: gcloud, Terraform, the client libraries and the console are all clients of the same APIs. {{clients}} Ask gcloud to show its requests, and creating a topic turns out to be a PUT of its name to its own address. {{put}} So curl can do the same. A subscription is one PUT. Against Google, the only difference is a header with a token. {{curl}} And Google's refusal, read without any tool in the way, is the one every tool in this course has quoted. {{refusal}} A client library is that API in your program's language, with retries, batching and pages handled for you. {{library}} You will publish with the library and read the messages back with curl. Same service, either side. {{same}} The library finds its own credentials, in a fixed order: a variable, then a file gcloud writes, then the metadata server. {{adc}} On your laptop it finds nothing, and says so. Point it at lesson 9's file, and it follows the federation as far as a laptop can. {{end}}
